videos.t: Using a Thai machete to badly smash open a coconut
videos.desc:
I’m staying on my friend Bua’s coconut farm in Thailand and I’m making some films. While waiting for my camera battery to charge, I shot this little clip of me using a cool Thai machete to open a coconut from their farm. 

‪The coconut is largely out of shot, I’m all sweaty and gross, and I did a pretty bad job ... but I think it’s pretty fun anyway so here goes.  ‬

Machetes are pretty cool tools.

videos.t: Prototype DIY sonic circuit sculpture⚡️filthy bass sounds and handmade electronics 🔥
videos.desc:
Here’s my latest strange circuit. It’s a sculpture made with brass and solder, triggering dirty synthy bass with capacitive touch. 

Speakers all the way up!!

Part of a new collaboration with Drew Fustini & Andrew Hockey, powered by Bela, BeagleBone and Pure Data.

videos.t: Prototype melodic DIY sonic circuit sculpture harp ⚡️ beautiful sounds from an otherworldly body
videos.desc:
Another strange circuit. A sculpture made with steel and solder, triggering gentle synth harp tones using capacitive touch. 

Speakers on! 

Part of a series, made in collaboration with Andrew Hockey and Drew Fustini, powered by Bela, BeagleBone and Pure Data.

videos.t: Sonic creature: melodic harp circuit sculpture
videos.desc:
Here's me playing one of my sonic creatures. This creature is a melodic harp circuit sculpture that I designed and built in 12 hours at a hack session with some other electronic music nerd friends. The first prototype was made at Music Tech Fest Frankfurt, then we made it a bit less scruffy (and a lot less prone to crashing) in the little workshop in the corner of my kitchen in Berlin. 

Andrew Hockey designed the sound. It is tuned to C minor and has a three octave range from left to right.

Materials: steel wire, solder and paper. 
Technologies: Capacitive Touch, Bela, BeagleBone Black and P

Now with tremelo and variable note length! 

Here's me playing one of my sonic creatures. This creature is a bass circuit sculpture that I designed and built a half day hack session. It was made in the little workshop in the corner of my kitchen in Berlin. 

Andrew Hockey designed the sound. It has a range of one octave, is tuned to C minor and the rightmost limbs trigger two effects: a tremelo and a delay. 

Materials: brass rods, solder and paper. 
Technologies: Capacitive Touch, Bela Mini, Pocket Beagle and Pure Data.

videos.t: My favourite technologies to teach with
videos.desc:
For Make Magazine's Maker Education teacher workshop at Makerfaire. 

I talk about the tech I use all the time in my classrooms. Featuring...

Going further with Physical Computing

videos.t: Music hacking & soft electronics! Short talk at Raspberry Pint about some of my recent projects
videos.desc:
Just me, chatting about some of the noisy squishy things I've made in the last year or so. I talk about my favourite tech to use for making embedded instruments (spoiler alert: Bela, Pure Data, micro:bit) and also geek out over embroidered electronics and flex PCBs from OSH Park. 

I gave this short talk at a Raspberry Pint meet up on Zoom in April 2020. Apologies for the shoddy video quality, my internet in Berlin is appalling. 

If you want to know more of my thoughts on music tech stuff, check out the livestream I did last week over on the Molten Music Tech channel: https://www.youtube.com/

videos.t: I made a soft, cuddly tentacle that purrs when you stroke it
videos.desc:
I made a soft, kind creature that helps me feel less anxious. 

I designed the weight, texture and sound of the creature to be comforting, but I also wanted to share how calming the making process itself is to me. 

This project works using a Bare Conductive board with a single sample loaded onto the SD card. This sample is triggered by me stroking the machine embroidered conductive thread that runs down the middle of my creature.
